text:
Every Jets game this season is played in the shadow of who isn't there. Connor Hellebuyck forced his way to New Jersey in October, and Stuart Skinner has inherited the net: .883 with 1.1 goals saved above expected, perfectly fine and nothing more. What Winnipeg has instead is a forward group having fun. Mark Scheifele is rewriting the franchise record books, Kyle Connor reached 700 career points, Dawson Mercer is settling in after his move, and Josh Morrissey won Thursday's game against the Islanders in overtime. Four wins in five, 22 goals for.

The catch is the chances. The Jets have only 47% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances), and they are without Dylan DeMelo and Isak Rosen. Our playoff race has them at 31%, which tells you the hot run hasn't erased a slow start.

Vegas is the mirror image. The Golden Knights are winless in four (0-1-3) and have been outscored 17-11, yet they took 56% of the expected goals in those games. That is a team getting robbed, not a team in trouble, and they still sit at 96% to make the playoffs. Adin Hill has been better than his .898 suggests, 3.8 goals saved above expected over his last five. Ivan Barbashev is back on the top line after an experiment elsewhere, and Victor Olofsson has 11 points in ten in his second Vegas stint.

The personal story is Mark Stone, who just set the Golden Knights' franchise points record and comes home to Winnipeg, where he grew up. Mitch Marner is one assist from 600, Nino Niederreiter one point from 500, Alex Iafallo one from 300. The special-teams matchup is worth watching: the Vegas power play creates 0.76 expected goals a game and the Jets' kill allows 0.81.
headline: Winnipeg's goalie after Hellebuyck faces a stuck Vegas
